title: Lolo’s Little Bridge
description: Ada and Bruno try a new idea to help Lolo cross a puddle.

cover.alt: Ada and Bruno watch Lolo cross a bark bridge.

illustration.alt: Ada and Bruno greet Lolo; a puddle separates him from a green leaf.

lines: Ada the rabbit is walking with Bruno the turtle when they meet their friend Lolo.
The little snail is following the garden path.
blocks.title: Three friends

lines: A plant with broad green leaves grows beyond a puddle.
Lolo stretches his eyestalks towards it, eager to reach a tasty leaf.
blocks.title: The goal

lines: Water fills the path, and Lolo stops at its edge.
The leaf looks close, but he has no dry way to reach it yet.
blocks.title: The puddle

lines: Ada kneels beside Lolo while Bruno looks around for something useful.
A big yellow leaf on the grass catches his eye.
blocks.title: The yellow leaf

variants.retryFeedback: Follow the path from Lolo to the green leaf.

variants.prompt: Where is the leaf Lolo wants?
variants.retryFeedback: Follow the path from Lolo to the green leaf.

illustration.alt: They test a yellow leaf as a bridge; it bends and they remove it.

lines: Bruno lifts the fallen leaf with both hands and looks it over.
It seems large enough to reach from one bank to the other.
blocks.title: Picking it up

lines: Together, the friends lay the leaf across the puddle, with an end on each side.
It looks like a little bridge for Lolo.
blocks.title: Over the water

lines: Before Lolo gets on, Bruno presses the middle with one finger.
The leaf sags into the water; it will not hold its shape.
blocks.title: It bends

lines: Ada lifts out the wet leaf and sets it on the grass.
Bruno points to a fallen log where they might find something stronger.
blocks.title: Looking for something else

variants.prompt: What happens to the yellow leaf?
variants.correctFeedback: That’s it! It bends into the water.
variants.retryFeedback: Look at the middle of the leaf when Bruno presses it.

variants.prompt: Why does Bruno test the leaf first?

options.text: To see if it works as a bridge

variants.correctFeedback: That’s it! To see if it works as a bridge.
variants.retryFeedback: Look at the middle of the leaf when Bruno presses it.

illustration.alt: They collect bark and two stones and prepare the supports on the banks.

lines: Beside the log, Ada finds a loose piece of bark that is broad and long.
She picks it up to take back to the puddle.
blocks.title: The bark

lines: Bruno finds two flat stones and takes one in each hand.
They will use them to support the ends of their new bridge.
blocks.title: The stones

lines: The friends carry their materials back along the path.
Lolo is waiting on the same bank and watches them come closer.
blocks.title: Coming back

lines: Bruno puts one stone on each bank, making sure both sit on dry ground.
Ada holds the bark ready for the next step.
blocks.title: The supports

variants.prompt: How many stones does Bruno pick up?
variants.retryFeedback: Look at Bruno’s hands and both sides of the puddle.

variants.prompt: Where do they put the stones?

options.text: In the middle of the water

variants.correctFeedback: That’s it! One on each dry bank.
variants.retryFeedback: Look at Bruno’s hands and both sides of the puddle.

illustration.alt: They place the bark, test the bridge, and Lolo begins to climb onto it.

lines: Together, they rest the bark across the two stones, leaving the middle above the water.
The dry banks are now connected.
blocks.title: The bridge

lines: Bruno tests the middle, just as he tested the yellow leaf.
This time, the bark stays straight instead of dipping into the puddle.
blocks.title: It holds

lines: Ada checks one end while Bruno checks the other.
Both are firmly supported, so they make room for Lolo to start crossing.
blocks.title: Checking it

lines: Lolo stretches his body onto the bark and slowly climbs up.
His friends move aside and watch as he begins the journey.
blocks.title: Lolo climbs on

variants.prompt: What happens when Bruno tests the bark?
variants.retryFeedback: Compare this bridge with the yellow leaf that bent.

variants.prompt: What do they do before Lolo climbs on?
variants.retryFeedback: Compare this bridge with the yellow leaf that bent.

illustration.alt: Lolo crosses, eats a leaf, and an ant also uses the bridge.

lines: Halfway across, Lolo keeps gliding towards the green leaf.
Water lies beneath him, and his friends wait patiently on the bank.
blocks.title: Crossing

lines: The front of his body reaches dry ground on the far side.
He slides a little farther until he is completely off the bridge.
blocks.title: Made it

lines: Lolo reaches the plant and takes a small bite from a green leaf.
After all that effort, he enjoys his garden snack.
blocks.title: The reward

lines: An ant discovers the bridge and crosses it while the three friends watch.
Their work has made a path for another little visitor.
blocks.title: Another visitor

variants.retryFeedback: Look at the tiny visitor and remember what the friends changed.

variants.prompt: What helped them solve the problem?
variants.correctFeedback: That’s it! Trying a new material together.
variants.retryFeedback: Look at the tiny visitor and remember what the friends changed.

rabbit.definition: An animal with long ears that hops.
rabbit.example: A wild rabbit hopped across the backyard early this morning.

turtle.definition: An animal with a protective shell.
turtle.example: The turtle at the pond takes forever to cross from one side to the other.

snail.definition: A small animal that glides along with a shell on its back.
snail.example: After the rain, several snails appeared on the sidewalk.

puddle.definition: A small pool of water on the ground.
puddle.example: We jumped over the puddles on our way to school.

bark.definition: The outer covering of a tree trunk.
bark.example: A beetle slowly crawled along the bark of the old tree.

bank.definition: The ground at the edge of water.
bank.example: We left our sandals on the bank of the river before wading in.

bridge.definition: A way across a gap or water.
bridge.example: We crossed the bridge to reach the other side of the park faster.

firmly.example: He checked that the ladder was firmly in place before climbing.

ant.definition: A small insect with six legs.
ant.example: A line of ants carried crumbs across the sidewalk.

materials.example: We bought the materials to build a small wooden box.

support.example: Two strong poles support the old wooden bridge.

patiently.example: She waited patiently while her brother tied his shoes.

eyestalks.definition: Long parts that carry a snail’s eyes.
eyestalks.example: The snail's eyestalks stretched out to feel the air around it.
